title: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter suspended two games for accepting agent-funded flight
dek: The NCAA suspended Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter for two games after he accepted a $427 flight from an agent following his declaration for the NFL draft. Carter repaid the agent and disengaged from representation in January. The university appealed the original three-game penalty and secured a reduction to two games.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Carter will miss Tennessee's season opener against Furman on Sept. 5 and the road game at Georgia Tech on Sept. 12, becoming eligible to return Sept. 19 against Kennesaw State.
bottom_line: Carter's two-game absence tests Tennessee's linebacker depth early in the season, though the team will have Campbell and Spillman available. The broader question of how the NCAA enforces agent contact rules on returning draft-eligible players remains open as more cases emerge across college football.
body: Tennessee linebacker Arion Carter will miss the Volunteers' first two games of the 2026 season after the NCAA suspended him for accepting a $427 flight from an agent following his declaration for the NFL draft, according to ESPN's reporting.

The suspension stems from Carter's interaction with agent representation after announcing his draft intention. Carter, a senior from Smyrna, Tennessee, disengaged from the agent and repaid him for the flight in January, per ESPN.

The NCAA originally imposed a three-game suspension. Tennessee appealed the penalty and the NCAA reduced it to two games. Carter will be ineligible for the Sept. 5 opener against Furman and the Sept. 12 road game at Georgia Tech, and will become eligible to return for the Sept. 19 matchup against Kennesaw State.

Coach Josh Heupel issued a statement saying Carter disengaged from the agent and repaid him, and that the team disagrees with the NCAA's ruling. Heupel also noted that Carter will graduate from Tennessee in public health with Dean's List honors in August.

Carter recorded 76 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and one fumble recovery in the 2025 season, according to ESPN. He played through a foot injury late in that season, aggravated it after declaring for the draft, underwent surgery, and chose to return to Tennessee for another year rather than pursue the NFL.
Tennessee's linebacker room includes former Penn State transfer Amare Campbell and freshman All-American Edwin Spillman, who led the Vols with 81 tackles in 2025.

The case raises unresolved questions about which specific NCAA bylaws governed Carter's suspension and whether similar enforcement has been applied to other draft-eligible players in comparable circumstances.
